newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise for sixth straight session.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise for sixth straight session.

text.p: Ignoring political uncertainty, French shares finished higher on Friday for the sixth straight trading day, helped by a strong performance by Wall Street.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed near the day's best levels, finishing up 1.06 percent or 28.40 points at 2,719.25 while the CAC-40 futures contract rose 16 points to 2,707.
The CAC-40 index has risen nearly 200 points since Sunday's parliamentary election vaulted the Socialists into power in an alliance with the Communist Party and Greens.
The market seesawed after release of mixed U.S jobs data showed lower than expected job creations but a fall in the May jobless rate to 4.8 percent, the lowest level since October 1973.
The low jobless rate in the United States contrasted starkly with German figures showing a seasonally adjusted 11.4 percent of Germans out of work in May compared with 11.2 percent in April.
The market picked up renewed strength as Wall Street powered ahead. The French market was also helped by a stronger dollar.
Dealers said the market was split between those who believed the new government posed no threat to shares and those who feared its policies could be harmful to investor interests.
"We'll know more about the government's policies next week," said one. He said this week's rise had been underpinned by U.S. buying with consumer-oriented stocks particularly in favour.

Retailer Pinault-Printemps finished up 3.50 percent at 2,630 francs in strong volume of 76,621 shares traded after reporting sales to end May up 7.6 percent. Brokerage Meeschaert Rousselle put the shares on a strong buy rating with a price target of 2,900-3,000 by year end.

But shares in semiconductor group SGS-Thomson Microelectronics slumped 5.52 percent to 445.0 francs after the company issued a profit warning. The company said second-quarter profit was likely to be within a range approximating first-quarter earnings of $0.65 per share.
